root_cause.text: The function `snd_ctl_elem_init_enum_names()` fails to check if `buf_len` has become zero before calling `strnlen()` on the remaining pointer, allowing a call to `strnlen(p, 0)` which, under `CONFIG_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, triggers a panic because the fortified `strnlen()` checks the object size against an unknown adjusted pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "If buf_len reaches zero but items remain, the next iteration calls strnlen(p, 0). While strnlen(p, 0) returns 0 and would hit the existing name_len == 0 error path, CONFIG_FORTIFY_SOURCE's fortified strnlen() first checks maxlen against __builtin_dynamic_object_size(). When Clang loses track of p's object size inside the loop, this triggers a BRK exception panic before the return value is examined." The patch adds a `buf_len == 0` guard at the loop entry to prevent this scenario.

intent_record.what: Added a conditional check at the beginning of the loop in snd_ctl_elem_init_enum_names that checks if buf_len is zero. If true, it frees the names buffer and returns -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when buf_len is zero, the function will immediately free the names buffer and return an error, preventing further processing of enumeration items. This avoids relying on the subsequent strnlen call with zero length (which would also trigger the error) and makes the behavior explicit.
